26 And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: - Romans 11:26 (KJV)

 God made many Old Testament prophecies about the nation of Israel and you can be sure they will all come to pass. This verse has been taught that all the Jews will be saved in the end times, but that is not what Paul is saying. It also is not saying that they all will come to believe in Jesus as their Savior, as that is not what is shown in Revelations. I believe what Paul is saying, is that a remnant of all the Tribes of Israel will be saved, as Paul had just been talking about God always saving a remnant of the Jews (Romans 11:2-5) by election. This Deliverer, I believe, is the Angel that goes down to the earth (Revelations 7:2-8), and puts the seal of God on 144,000 Jews, and it shows that there were 12,000 from each of the 12 tribes of Israel that God saves by election. This fulfills the promises that God has made to the nation of Israel, to not ever let any of the tribes be totally extinguished.

 I had never been able to understand this verse before, and so I asked God about it as I was studying the book of Romans, and the Holy Spirit gave me the above information. Once you realize that Israel is referring to the tribes and not the Jewish people individually, then it makes it understandable, and what Paul is saying is that all the tribes of Israel will have a remnant saved, as God has promised. I believe this is what this verse is saying, and praise God for the Holy Spirit (John 14:26) to help us understand His Word.

Capital punishment has its place. There are some individuals who are just too far gone to rehabilitate. Either through extensive mental trauma, or simple biology (psychopaths), they will continue to hurt others.

The problem is always a matter of ensuring only the deserving are dispatched, which is nigh impossible to ensure with current technology and legal methods.

Even so, does that mean we need to be cruel in the administration of said punishment? No. There are plenty of ways to ensure a painless death. The problem is, they do not get implemented because some people believe that the condemned should suffer. What these people do not realise, or perhaps do and just don't care, is that the punishment is the death itself, not how it is carried out.

After they are dead, they are dead. No more life, no more chances to either hurt or contribute to society. Their existence is over. It is the ultimate form of punishment.

So instead of worrying about how much or little a criminal suffers in their final hours, please instead consider the well being of the executioners, and what effect it is having on them to carry out such painful punishments.
